questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to have courses that matched my academic interest and the university had to be located somewhere that allowed me to travel easily.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was completely different from how things are done in KU, but the administrative office at Stirling was were helpful and would always answer me emails, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid, it was very restrictive, but I also arrived in July so I mostly recieved help from the people I was living with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I had already found some websites, but when I asked the Stirling study abroad, they also provided me with websites and tips.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check the travel distance, because the public transport here can be expensive and the roads are not the best for cycling. Also always do multiple interviews with the person you are renting a room from and ask a lot of questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, if I had any questions I simply emailed my host university and they helped me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mostly relied on the teachers I had at my host university, but you are asked if you have certain conditions that require assistance, etc. and they are very good at helping students with special needs.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sue to check whether it says spring or autumn.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were very intense with the amount of weekly reading, and it can feel overwhelming that the exam papers are written during the semester instead of after the end of the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid, everything was different from their normal teaching. Some courses were only online, some courses posted lecture videos online and had seminars at the campus.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ARTU9H5 - Death, Disease and Disability: The State and the Hazardous Working Environment 1800-1914
ENGU9EH - History of the English Language
ENGU9EV - Victorian Literature and Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like linguistics then the History of the English Language course is fantastic as it teaches you parts of the English language that have never been focused on at KU. However, you do need a good grammatical, phonetic, and linguistic foundation, since the course does not focus on teaching those aspects, only the different language periods.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The train tickets and the Covis test kit I had to buy when I came to the UK. I had to pay around £75 for two tests I had to take on day 2 and day 8 whilst I self-isolated for 10 days.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is less expensive than I thought it would be when their prices are reduced.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid it was difficult, but the English department had an event over Halloween and over Christmas.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs you can sign up for and there is something for everybody.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit as many places in Scotland as you can, it is all worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk with them before or after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything particularly difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring books from previous semesters that might help you (grammar books, novels, etc.).
Warm clothes and waterproof outerwear. 
Snacks and food to help you get through self-isolation since online orders can be very expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to ask the teachers about the structure of a paper since they measure word count, not anslag, and sometimes they assignments that are not traditional essays. Also, ask if you can use them as a reference on your CV.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To push my academic boundaries with courses that were more specific than in KU.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload in the history department is very different from what I was used to at KU. Also I had to write my exam papers during the semester so the balance between doing the weekly studying and the exam papers was very difficult.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
